item.title: FC Dallas ride second-half surge to Game 1 win over Portland Timbers
item.description: FC Dallas ride second-half surge to Game 1 win over Portland Timbers By Ari Liljenwall FC Dallas struck twice in quick succession early in the second half before adding a late insurance goal to earn a 3-0 victory over the Portland Timbers in Game 1 of their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series at Toyota Stadium on Saturday. The result gives Dallas a 1-0 series lead heading into Game 2 at Providence Park on Nov. 28, where another victory would send them through to the Western Conference Semifinals. After a scoreless opening 45 minutes, Dallas broke through in the 53rd minute when Petar Musa sprung Daniel Job into space. Job's initial effort was saved by Portland goalkeeper James Pantemis , but Joaquín Valiente pounced on the rebound to open the scoring. Just two minutes later, Job beat his defender and delivered a low cross that Valiente finished through Pantemis' legs to complete his rapid-fire brace. Substitute Sam Sarver iced the match in the fourth minute of second-half stoppage time, finishing off a feed from fellow sub Logan Farrington to put the result beyond doubt. item.title: Donald Trump sparks outrage with comments on Barry Bonds
item.description: Credit: USA Today network via Reuters President Donald Trump has spent the last year championing Pete Rose and Roger Clemens for the Baseball Hall of Fame. But when he was asked about Barry Bonds on Saturday, his argument fell apart pretty quickly. Calling in to Fox News, Trump insisted that Bonds’ case is “different” from Clemens’, even though both players were accused of using performance-enhancing drugs. As he tried to explain the difference, Trump eventually landed on the claim that Bonds “just looked like he took drugs,” a comment which quickly sparked outrage. ‘It’s different’ Trump called in to Saturday in America , the Fox News show hosted by his former press secretary Kayleigh McEnany. McEnany, whose husband Sean Gilmartin is a former New York Mets pitcher, told Trump that her husband and her soon-to-be brother-in-law believe Bonds belongs in Cooperstown. Trump has long pushed for Rose, who was made eligible for the Hall after his death, and he issued Rose a full pardon for his 1990 tax conviction on Thursday. He has also called Clemens, a vocal supporter of his, one of the greatest pitchers ever. But Trump drew a line with Bonds, at least at first. “Well, it’s different. Pete didn’t take drugs. And Pete was Charlie Hustle,” Trump said . He then pointed out that Clemens has always denied using steroids, before seemingly realizing that Bonds has done the same. “And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs. Barry Bonds, I think, said that too. But a lot of— I mean, look, he was such a great player. You know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place. But I think, and I’ll have to look at it, and I’ll consider what you’re saying too, by the way. He was— I watched him. The problem is he just looked like he took drugs. I mean, you know. item.title: East Stroudsburg football defeats Assumption, earns first NCAA playoff win since 2005
item.description: EAST STROUDSBURG – For the first time in over 20 years, East Stroudsburg University football will advance in the NCAA Division II playoffs. The Warriors put together a stout defensive effort, defeating Assumption 24-3 inside Eiler-Martin Stadium to earn their first playoff win since 2005, when head coach Jimmy Terwilliger was in uniform and leading the program to a regional championship in 2005. “This joy that I had as a player 20-something years ago, I remember very fondly,” Terwilliger said. “One of my goals here as a football coach is to give the same joy to our players. So, to be able to pull off a playoff victory at home is something I cherish.” The final score is a tad misleading as both teams struggled to move the ball for most of the game, but the difference was a player many were pleasantly surprised to see: Harrison Susi, who started the year as QB1 before Matt Machalik took over. Susi’s number was called in some red zone and running packages, and the first impression was rough, throwing an interception in the red zone in the first quarter. But he redeemed himself later, breaking free on a direct snap for a 41-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter. For a while, it appeared that would be the only touchdown of the game, until Susi delivers a dagger for his second rushing touchdown of the game late in the fourth quarter. Susi ended the game with 103 rushing yards on 11 carries, averaging 9.4 yards per attempt. “I trust Harrison Susi to make big-time plays in big-time situations,” Terwilliger said. “Today, the game called for Harrison to be able to come in and be plus-one in the box. “When the ball is in his hands, great things can happen for 13.” Ty Quintos also contributed two field goals over the course of the game, and after Susi’s second score and a defensive stop, many thought the final would be 17-3. item.title: Dolphins Activate Baker, Roster Moves Signal Shift
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins moved on Saturday to fix their secondary before facing the Buffalo Bills. The team activated cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. from the physically unable to perform list, clearing his path to play this Sunday. This decision removes him from the injury report entirely, according to Sports Illustrated . The front office added a player while removing a veteran kicker to make room for him. Zane Gonzalez is gone after missing two field goals and an extra point in the loss to the Colts. Daniel Carlson takes over the kicking duties, while Jack Browning handles punting duties from the practice squad. Defensive Depth Remains a Major Concern The roster math tells a story of thinning options along the defensive line. Three defensive tackles—Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers—landed on the injured reserve list, leaving the team with only three active players at that spot. Kenneth Grant, Keith Cooper Jr., and Jordan Jefferson are the only names left to stop the run. The team might have to use edge defenders like Malik Herring or Eric Watts in the middle to fill the gap. Watts is the only player on the official roster listed as a defensive end. This lack of depth forces the coaching staff to get creative with their lineup on Sunday. The addition of Baker Jr. brings the total number of active cornerbacks to six. That is a high number for any team, but it makes sense given the injury issues. The Dolphins also carry ten offensive linemen and six wide receivers on the active roster. These numbers show a team trying to protect its starters while staying ready for a rough game. The Bills face similar issues with their own injury report, listing Ed Oliver as questionable with an oblique injury. Dorian Williams and Christian Benford are already out, and Dalton Kincaid is doubtful. A Critical Matchup at Highmark Stadium Sunday’s game will test the Dolphins’ ability to handle a depleted roster against a tough opponent. The Bills are likely to hold some injured players back to stay healthy for the Thanksgiving night game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Miami has to win this game without the luxury of a full defense. The team waived Gonzalez after he struggled in the 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Dolphins will elevate Carlson and Browning for the game, with Carlson allowed to be elevated a maximum of three times before a permanent roster move is required. The next game is set for Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium.

For years, the San Francisco Giants have flatly refused to engage or listen to any trade inquiries involving franchise cornerstone Logan Webb . That era is officially over. Following a frustrating 2026 campaign, San Francisco is open to listening to offers for its three-time All-Star right-hander. At 30 years old, Webb immediately becomes the top starting pitcher available on the winter market outside of free-agent left-hander Tarik Skubal. While Webb posted a 4.31 ERA across 27 starts in 2026, his 3.45 FIP signals he pitched far better than his surface numbers indicate. Between 2023 and 2025, Webb eclipsed 204.2 innings every season and led baseball with 224 strikeouts in 2025. With two years remaining on an ultra-affordable five-year, $90 million contract paying him $23 million in 2027 and $24 million in 2028, Webb is the ultimate pivot for contenders unwilling or unable to pay Skubal’s record-shattering price tag. item.title: Key Barcelona star to be benched vs Villarreal
item.description: Key Barcelona star to be benched vs Villarreal A leading member of the defensive ranks at La Liga giants Barcelona is expected to be rested for the club’s post-international break return to action against Villarreal. Hansi Flick’s troops are of course primed to kick the defence of their Spanish top-flight title back into gear on Sunday afternoon. The Blaugrana head into proceedings with sights firmly on a three-point haul, having been joined at the summit of the table by arch rivals Real Madrid on Saturday night. As alluded to above, though, in efforts towards as much, Barca look set to make do without arguably their most important defensive figure. Drawn on Pau Cubarsí’s status to face Villarreal after the youngster suffered a minor fitness setback whilst on international duty with Spain, the German tactician went on to admit: ”We’ll take care of Cubarsí, and the most likely scenario is that he’ll rest tomorrow. We’ll see what we do with him for Baku (against Sabah).” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Viral Georgia Tech couple goes through relationship turmoil as Jesse Palmer breaks it down
item.description: Saturday’s Wake Forest – Georgia Tech game was a blowout, but it produced a hilarious fourth-quarter moment. With Wake Forest up 50-22, ESPN’s camera panned to a couple in the stands, seemingly in a heated debate. Even ESPN’s Jesse Palmer , the game’s color commentator, found it hilarious. MORE: Arch Manning gives strong hint on 2027 NFL Draft decision “The playoff situation is intense right now, maybe not as intense as this conversation,” Palmer said . This is Palmer’s expertise, since he hosts ABC’s “The Bachelor” and was the show’s lead in 2004. He later added more thoughts to the argument. “He is locked in,” Palmer said. “He is holding her to court right now. He wants an answer, and he’s not leaving. I mean, they are in each other’s personal space. He’s not happy with whatever she just told him.” Here’s the full exchange: A Georgia Tech couple appears to have a breakup live on air and the commentators analyze and break it down #StingEm #GoDeacs pic.twitter.com/CQukZ1DRJD — Carter Lowe (@carterl0we) November 21, 2026 What happened after? Oct 14, 2023; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; Sportscaster Jesse Palmer talks before a game between the LSU Tigers and the Auburn Tigers at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Later in the fourth quarter, the camera panned back to the couple, who made up with a few kisses. It was the game’s comeback. Update: They made up!! https://t.co/iSgaeD9Be0 pic.twitter.com/g7JGC2DH0h — Carter Lowe (@carterl0we) November 21, 2026 Sometimes, all you gotta do is talk things out, even if it gets aired on national television. As for the actual game, Wake Forest won 50-29, improving to 10-1 overall and inching closer to a potential College Football Playoff spot. Wake Forest will play Duke next week and is on the brink of playing for the ACC title. item.title: James Talarico fires cannon, chats with cheerleaders on Texas football sideline
item.description: Senator James Talarico greets Texas cheerleaders as he attends the Texas v. Arkansas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Texas' new soon-to-be senator enjoyed a victory lap on the Texas football sideline Saturday. James Talarico , who defeated Ken Paxton in November to become Texas' first Democrat senator since 1993, spent time near the field at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium before the Longhorns hosted Arkansas. Talarico was joined by his girlfriend, Brianna Menard. The two chatted with Texas cheerleaders pregame, and Talarico took part in a classic Longhorns tradition as he stood behind and fired Smokey the Cannon. GOLDEN: How the hell did the Texas Longhorns win that? The hard way. FILM REVIEW: How Arch Manning's legs saved Longhorns at LSU Saturday marked Talarico's first time at DKR this season, though he's watched each contest this season, per his office. Talarico also attended a Texas home game in 2025, and he shared a brief comment on his appearance Saturday through a spokesperson. "Hook 'em horns." Senator James Talarico fires Smokey the Cannon as he attends the Texas v. Arkansas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. item.description: Peyton Miller dazzles in playoff debut with New England Revolution By José Nuñez Welcome to the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, Peyton Miller . The New England Revolution 's rising homegrown star stole the show during Saturday's Round One opener, causing an own goal and scoring a superb volley to secure a 2-0 Game 1 win over the Philadelphia Union at Gillette Stadium. “I think that just shows how much he has grown in maturity, if I can say it like that. It really shows that he is ready to compete,” head coach Marko Mitrović said of Miller's standout effort. “Yes, he is a really young player, but he is converting from potential to being a performer. That is what a performer does.” Big first impression Miller memorable playoff debut marked another milestone in a season full of them for the 19-year-old. Amid producing a career-best 7g/9a, the versatile wingback broke into the US men's national team in September and placed sixth in the 2026 22 Under 22 rankings. And in New England's first playoff appearance in three years, Miller led the Revs to their first postseason victory since 2020. “It’s surreal playing for my boyhood club, so I’m just thankful for everything and all glory to God. I thank the fans for all the support today," said Miller, who became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in playoff history. "My parents, my friends, are all here, so this is special.” On to Philadelphia Miller and the Revolution can close out Round One when the Best-of-3 Series moves to Philadelphia's Subaru Park for Game 2 on Nov. 28 (4:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). However, they're not taking anything for granted. That especially applies against an opponent that was dominant throughout the second half of the season behind the inspired play of teenage phenom Cavan Sullivan , Golden Boot presented by Audi contender Milan Iloski and others. “Philadelphia is a very demanding team, a team that keeps you on your toes for all 90 minutes," warned Mitrović. "Those games with Philly are always games of margins, and we just have to ensure that those margins go on our side.” WATCH: Peyton Miller & Revs take Game 1 vs. Philadelphia

item.title: Bengals' DB fined for taunting penalty vs Steelers
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle was fined $11,941 for unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting during the second quarter of their NFL Week 10 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . NBC Sports analyst and former Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth was critical of Battle for the penalty. Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss in 2025. item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Roman Wilson #10 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 21: Roman Wilson #10 of the Pittsburgh Steelers enters the field before the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 1: Nick Herbig #51 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) Getty Both the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburgh Steelers are going to get reinforcements in the passing game on Sunday. On the Steelers’ side, the team officially activated their wideout, Roman Wilson. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Wilson is no longer on the injured reserve, and he’s set to play in Week 11. Roman Wilson’s Steelers Season Getty FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – SEPTEMBER 21: Roman Wilson #10 of the Pittsburgh Steelers enters the field before the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) The 2026 NFL season was shaping up to be a breakout year for Wilson. Throughout his first two seasons, he played in just 13 games. After missing most of his rookie effort, Wilson had just 166 yards to show for heading into the 2026 season. Before going out with a hand injury, Wilson appeared in five games for the Steelers. He was targeted 25 times, catching 14 passes for 188 yards and two touchdowns. After a Week 5 Steelers win over the Indianapolis Colts, Wilson was added to the injured reserve list. He will make his return to face the Eagles on the road. Pittsburgh’s Defense Takes A Hit Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 1: Nick Herbig #51 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) It’s not all positive for the Steelers. Shortly before it was revealed that Wilson was activated, it was reported that the Steelers were ruling out the edge rusher , Nick Herbig. As he deals with hip and rib injuries, Herbig was initially listed as questionable on the injury report against the Eagles. But the Steelers didn’t waste any more time. They officially ruled him out on Saturday afternoon. This season, Herbig has appeared in nine games. He racked up 3.0 sacks and produced 23 tackles, with seven going for a loss. While the Eagles’ secondary has another weapon to worry about, the offensive line won’t have to see Herbig, who is in the Steelers’ frontline rotation. item.title: Shawnee outlasts Chatham, claims Group 3 girls soccer title
item.description: FRANKLIN TOWNSHIP — Lucy Arps was one of the few Chatham players not crying after the NJSIAA Group 3 girls soccer final. The Cougars had lost to Shawnee, 3-2 in overtime, but Arps was focused on more than just the result. Despite winning the Morris County Tournament for six straight years and five consecutive sectional titles, Chatham came into the championship match feeling like underdogs. And that fire kept fueling the Cougars, even as they watched the Renegades celebrating on the field at Franklin High School. "Nobody expected us to get here," said Arps, a Chatham junior. "Going in, we were the underdogs, but that was our fuel, 100%. We live for that. ... You can't ask for anything better from us. It's just being smarter regarding those key moments at the end." It is the third time these teams have faced off in the Group final in four years. Chatham beat Shawnee on penalty kicks in 2023 and double OT in 2025. In between, the Renegades toppled Northern Highlands to win what had been their only Group title. On Nov. 21, they captured their second on an improbable far-post, top-corner goal from senior Madison Zaun with 1:16 to play in overtime. All three Shawnee (23-2-1) goals came within the last two minutes of a period. Sophomore Sloan Ludwig put a bicycle kick into the top corner, converting senior Julia Ford's 45-yard free kick. At the time, it tied the match 1-1 heading into halftime. Ludwig also tied the game again with 1:37 left in regulation on a shot from 25 yards out that flew into the top right corner. "It was an indescribable feeling," Ludwig said. "I'm so excited to share this moment with my team. This is the best feeling I could ask for, and the best moment I could have." More: 2026 Northwest Jersey Athletic Conference girls soccer honors Junior midfielder Emily Piskadlo had a goal and an assist, opening the scoring midway through the first half on Chatham's first shot of the match. Senior Sophie D'Egidio put the Cougars (16-6-2) back on top with 16:48 left in regulation. Shawnee coach Drew Wagner pulled sophomore goalkeeper Lacey Abrams with about four minutes left to put on an extra field player. Wagner complimented Chatham's ball movement through the midfield as "the things that he tries to do, a big compliment to the girls," according to head coach Anthony Correale. It is the first time Chatham had allowed more than one goal in a NJSIAA Tournament match, finishing the postseason with 16 goals scored and just four given up. "When that happens, it's just meant to be for them," Correale said. "We just got beat on a long ball, and that was that, you know? It's a tough pill to swallow." item.title: Purdue football didn't just lose to Wisconsin, the Boilermakers gave up
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − The losses we've come to accept, but what transpired in Purdue football 's final home game of 2026 was so much worse. The Boilermakers quit. You can question talent, coaching, scheme or a myriad of other reasons for Purdue 's lack of success, but competitiveness was never one Barry Odom worried about. Until Saturday. Wisconsin's 42-10 victory over the Boilermakers at Ross-Ade Stadium, the Badgers ' 19th straight in the series, came in a game that was very much up in the air late in the second quarter, when Purdue trailed 21-10 and had the ball. Come the fourth quarter, Purdue had rolled over. "I know I’m not supposed to let my mind wander, but in the fourth quarter, you look at that and I haven’t had that before," Odom said. "In 27 years, I have not. I’ve been beat, but not like today." With a fan base that showed its lack of support by the number of empty seats on a day where the weather was as beautiful as anyone could hope for in the third week of November. A number of the seats that were filled were occupied by fans in Wisconsin gear. More: Another failed outing for Purdue football vs Wisconsin: Grading the Boilers The faithful, who continued to show up desperately clinging to one more magic moment Purdue had seemed to capture in the middle of the season , instead were treated to a team that clearly didn't have the same Boilermaker pride as those fans. Anyone who endured Saturday's loss in its entirety who doesn't have a direct tie to someone within the Purdue football program should be commended. If they haven't checked out by now, they never will. So, Purdue football, give them something. "There’s a great foundation. I know it may not look like it," linebacker Charles Correa said. "There’s a lot of guys who believe in this program and believe in coach Odom, and he is going to put all the pieces in the right place." Correa is a team captain and, by all accounts, loves Purdue. He returned after playing for a 2-10 team last season because of it. Correa also loves winning, and he's a part of a team that not only isn't winning, but one that didn't even fight against a Wisconsin team that seemed ripe for the picking. The Badgers poured in their second-highest point total of the season, scoring more only against Eastern Michigan, and produced 508 yards. A Purdue offense that once hummed couldn't even muster 200, and its attempt to find a flaw in Wisconsin's defense backfired with an experimental offensive look starting Evans Chuba at quarterback. The Badgers didn't show the look Purdue hoped it would with Chuba behind center. On Purdue's next offensive series, it was down 14-0, and Ryan Browne was in a situation where he'd have to throw the Boilermakers back into it. Instead, Browne had statistically his worst game of the season. Aside from his first two drives, Purdue did nothing offensively. And the defense continued to look like what Purdue fans have unfortunately come to expect. Should we be surprised by Saturday's outcome? No

item.title: Bearcats bowl-eligble for a 2nd straight season, where do they go?
item.description: The Cincinnati Bearcats 35-28 win over Colorado gives them six wins and makes them bowl-eligible for the second straight season. Cole Tabb ran for 120 yards and two touchdowns and had seven receptions for 110 yards and two more scores. JC French IV, one of the 22 seniors playing their last game at Nippert, was 18-for-19 for 208 yards with two touchdown passes to Tabb plus 38 rushing yards and a score. “It means a ton, it's crazy," French said. "It's the last home game ever, a surreal moment. I am happy for the rest of these seniors.” UC has now qualified for a bowl bid in 14 of its last 19 seasons, including four New Year's Six bowls and the 2021 College Football Playoff semifinal appearance against Alabama in the Goodyear Cotton Bowl. Coming into the Nov. 21 game vs. Colorado , these were the bowl projections for the Bearcats: ESPN's Mark Schlabach – The Radiance Technologies Independence Bowl in Shreveport. The bowl is set for Dec. 22 on ESPN at 7:30 (Central)/8:30 (Eastern). Schlabach has UC playing Oregon State on ESPN. ESPN's Kyle Bonagura – Bonagura also sees UC in the Independence Bowl in Shreveport Dec. 22, but with a different matchup. He sees the Bearcats against the Washington Huskies on ESPN at 7:30 (Central)/8:30 (Eastern). USA Today – The Cactus Bowl in Tempe. This would be an interesting matchup for Bearcats fans as they have UC vs. Wisconsin. Potentially, it's Scott Satterfield vs. Luke Fickell at Mountain America Stadium with a 7:30 (Eastern) kickoff on ABC. New York Times/Athletic – Another Independence Bowl prediction Dec. 22 in Shreveport with an 8:30 (Eastern) kickoff on ESPN. They see the Bearcats against Stanford. UC is 10-13 all-time in bowl games but has dropped the last four (Peach Bowl, Cotton Bowl, Fenway Bowl, Liberty Bowl). The Bearcats last prevailed in a bowl game on Jan. 2, 2020, beating Boston College 38-6 in the Birmingham Bowl at Legion Field. item.title: NBA officials miss Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds late in Bucks' loss
item.description: PHILADELPHIA - The Milwaukee Bucks haven't had a lot go right for them during the course of this season, especially in the midst of a current 13-game losing streak following a 132-129 loss to Philadelphia at the Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov. 21. But they were on the receiving end of a brutal missed call that could have determined the outcome of the game in the final seconds. Trailing 130-129 with 4.8 seconds left, the 76ers were inbounding opposite of their bench following a timeout. All of the game referees were watching LeBron James inbound, and then positioned around the 76ers basket. Only James floated the inbound pass deep toward the opposite end to Joel Embiid, and as the big man collected the ball and tried to evade an intentional foul from Tyler Herro, he stepped out of bounds. Only no one was there to see it but the Bucks' bench, and the fans in that corner. No whistle was blown, and Herro eventually fouled Embiid with 1.5 seconds left. Though the Bucks did not have a challenge, that is not something that could be reviewed had Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins had one. "Well, Embiid, he did step out of bounds," Herro said. "But for ref, it is a tough play. 'Cause the ball was being taken out on the other side of the court. For him to see that you've got to have a ref on that baseline. So it was a tough call, a tough play to see as a ref. So, I get that one." Brayden Burries wasn't in that corner, but saw the video of the play later. "He was out of bounds, but you know, they're humans, they miss calls," Burries said. "It just so happened it was a crucial call. But, it's OK." While the officials did miss the call, it's what happened in the immediate moments afterward that inevitably hurt the Bucks even more. Herro was trailing Embiid trying to intentionally foul, but when he saw Embiid step out, he instinctively pulled up. As soon as he realized there was no whistle, he committed the foul with 1.5 seconds left. "It looked like Tyler thought, or the team, that he stepped out of bounds," Jaime Jaquez Jr. "I didn't even see what happened but obviously I believe him. I think he kind of like slowed down because he thought they were going to call it, but I don't think there were any refs on that side. Which is, weird. But, I don't know where they're supposed to be but that was an important view for them to take a look at. I don't know." Shortly thereafter, Herro's buzzer beating attempt to tie the game was ruled no good as the ball left his hand a split second too late. "I just had to get the shot off a little bit quicker," Herro said. "I thought I had a little bit more time. Coach drew up a great play for me. I had the shot I wanted, I made it, just gotta be able to get it off on time next time." item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
